content: 1. When initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, dose adjustments of calcifediol may be necessary. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact parathyroid hormone (PTH), and serum calcium concentrations should be closely monitored. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose and monitor closely during coadministration. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Carbamazepine decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, monitor for loss of virologic response. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the cariprazine dose during coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for dosage modification. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 8. Cenobamate decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed and monitor closely. 9. Cobicistat and ceritinib increase each other’s toxicity by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This combination may also increase the risk of QT prolongation. 10. Chloramphenicol increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of inhaled ciclesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily during coadministration and monitor for adverse effects. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 15. Clarithromycin increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended during coadministration with anticonvulsants. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the clorazepate dose if necessary and monitor closely. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to a significant increase in cobimetinib levels. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of colchicine. Coadministration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions. Dose adjustments may be necessary; refer to colchicine prescribing information. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conivaptan also increases cobicistat levels. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg and monitor closely. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the crizotinib dose to 250 mg daily and monitor for QT prolongation. 24. Cyclophosphamide increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely during coadministration. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration in patients with atrial fibrillation and CrCl <30 mL/min or in DVT/PE treatment with CrCl <50 mL/min. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dabrafenib decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Danazol increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dapsone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the darifenacin dose to 5 mg daily during coadministration and monitor closely. 32. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of darolutamide. Monitor for increased adverse reactions and adjust the darolutamide dose as needed when coadministered with P-gp and CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases cobicistat levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dasatinib dose as needed during coadministration and refer to prescribing information for guidance. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose during coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of desipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 37. Dexamethasone decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Long-term use of corticosteroids metabolized by CYP3A4 may increase the risk of systemic corticosteroid effects, including Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. A reduced diazepam dose may be required during coadministration. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of buccal diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of intranasal diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting P-gp efflux transporter. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs, adjust the dose by 30-50%, and monitor closely. 44. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions, such as acute ergot toxicity. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of intranasal dihydroergotamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended during coadministration with antiarrhythmics. 48. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the docetaxel dose by 50% if coadministration cannot be avoided. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 50. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response. 51. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during coadministration. 54. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dronedarone. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of serious interactions.
